audits.title: P013 Driving improvement through audit: impact of 2017 regional audit and survey upon giant cell arteritis services in 2020
audits.standard: BSR guidance on giant cell arteritis (revised)
audits.setting: Rheumatology services at 16 hospitals in northwest England (regional audit and survey)

cycle1.result: 14/16 sites responded; 2 sites had a GCA pathway; routine steroid leaflets 6/14 (43%); 1 site had a GCA database; 8 had a steroid taper protocol.

audits.intervention: 2017 audit and survey results fed back to sites and regionally; sites introduced GCA pathways, temporal artery ultrasound, steroid leaflets and local QI.

cycle2.result: 15/16 sites responded; 6 sites had a GCA pathway; temporal artery ultrasound 6/15 (40%); routine steroid leaflets 12/15 (80%); GCA database 4 (27%); steroid taper protocol 7.

audits.other_findings: 9/15 (60%) sites said the 2017 audit prompted changes. No change in steroid card provision; 8/15 (53%) reported COVID-19 harmed services, mainly access to diagnostics.
audits.citation: Sharp C, Little J, Shahbaz A, Wood E, Wig S, Watson P, et al.. P013 Driving improvement through audit: impact of 2017 regional audit and survey upon giant cell arteritis services in 2020. Rheumatology. 2021;60(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/rheumatology/keab247.012.

audits.title: P001 Audit on giant cell arteritis fast track clinic in Tayside
audits.standard: British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) GCA standards
audits.setting: GCA fast track clinic, NHS Tayside (Ninewells Hospital, Dundee)

cycle1.result: 70.8% seen by rheumatology within 24 hours; 50% with visual symptoms seen by ophthalmology within 24 hours; 89% given steroids within 24 hours; 80.8% had ultrasound or biopsy; written information, recurrence advice, CRP and bone protection documentation 100%.

audits.other_findings: 35% diagnosed with GCA; one patient lost vision while on steroids; immediate follow-up time was 6 weeks.
audits.citation: Subramanian D, Bhat S. P001 Audit on giant cell arteritis fast track clinic in Tayside. Rheumatology. 2022;61(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.

audits.title: P009 Navigating giant cell arteritis (GCA) service during and post COVID-19 pandemic: an audit of GCA care at North Bristol NHS Trust against the BSR quality standards
audits.setting: Rheumatology department, North Bristol NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Mean referral to specialist review 2.7 days; temporal artery biopsy 41%.

audits.intervention: Twice-weekly registrar-led hot clinics, ad hoc slots in on-call consultant clinics for GCA referrals, and increased vascular ultrasound capacity during the pandemic.

cycle2.result: Mean referral to specialist review 1.6 days; all had vascular ultrasound; temporal artery biopsy 7.5%. 33% diagnosed and treated as GCA.

audits.other_findings: 75% of referrals came from primary care. Planned improvements: steroid advice at referral, updated primary care guideline on urgent ophthalmology input, and a GCA review proforma.
audits.citation: Lim K, Shahriar I, Villar S, Sin F. P009 Navigating giant cell arteritis (GCA) service during and post COVID-19 pandemic: an audit of GCA care at North Bristol NHS Trust against the BSR quality standards. Rheumatology. 2023;62(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.051.

audits.title: P189 Giant cell arteritis: audit of a fast-track assessment pathway including the use of positron emission tomography-computed tomography as an early diagnostic tool
audits.standard: British Society for Rheumatology audit tool standards for suspected GCA
audits.setting: Rheumatology, University College London Hospitals, fast-track pathway including PET-CT

cycle1.result: All reviewed within 3 days (95% by next day); all started on corticosteroids with FBC and ESR; all with visual symptoms given high-dose steroids and ophthalmology review (60% same day); 95% had baseline glucose, 75% vitamin D checked, 70% DEXA; of confirmed GCA, 54% had documented written information and 77% safety-netting advice.

audits.other_findings: 76% had PET-CT (56% positive) and 95% temporal artery ultrasound (11% positive); 7 patients (33%) had negative ultrasound but positive PET-CT. Only 1 patient (4.8%) had temporal artery biopsy.
audits.citation: Ghosh A, Morris V, Voo S, Ludwig D. P189 Giant cell arteritis: audit of a fast-track assessment pathway including the use of positron emission tomography-computed tomography as an early diagnostic tool. Rheumatology. 2026;65(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.219.

audits.title: E158 A closed cycle audit of assessment of suspected giant cell arteritis at North Middlesex University Hospital
audits.standard: BSR and GIRFT guidelines for GCA assessment and management
audits.setting: Same Day Emergency Care, North Middlesex University Hospital (district general hospital), London

cycle1.result: Steroids 34%; rheumatology referral 55%; temporal artery ultrasound 15%; CRP 92%; median time to eye clinic 2 days.

audits.intervention: Trust SDEC GCA pathway guideline, streamlined temporal artery ultrasound order on IT system, local teaching, pathway poster in clinic rooms and Southend GCA probability score.

cycle2.result: Steroids 54%; rheumatology referral 77%; temporal artery ultrasound 77% (p < 0.001); CRP 100%; median time to eye clinic 1 day.

audits.other_findings: Time to rheumatology assessment did not change significantly (1 to 1.5 days). A GCA probability score >12 had an AUC of 0.978.
audits.citation: Ark R, Fardeen K, MacBrayne A. E158 A closed cycle audit of assessment of suspected giant cell arteritis at North Middlesex University Hospital. Rheumatology. 2026;65(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.379.
